{"id": "2:144/q01", "question": "What does qad nara convey?", "turns_on": "Whether qad itself conveys frequency, rarity, confirmation, or past reference.", "positions": [{"id": "2:144/q01/p1", "position": "Qad conveys frequent divine seeing.", "reasons": "KASHSHAF-FULL: Qad conveys frequent divine seeing. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī glosses قد نرى as perhaps we see and takes it to suggest abundant seeing, citing قد أترك القرن. Against: SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الشيخ): The shaykh says al-Zamakhsharī contradicts himself: ربما suggests rarity on the relevant account, not abundance; قد itself does not encode abundance, which comes from repeated turning being seen. BURHAN, d. 794 (جماعة من المتأخرين): Some later scholars assign قد an unusual sense of abundance; al-Zamakhsharī applies that reading to قد نرى تقلب وجهك. BURHAN, d. 794 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī takes قد in قد نرى to indicate frequent or abundant occurrence. ITQAN, d. 911 (الزمخشري): Sibawayh and others recognize an intensive sense of قد; al-Zamakhshari applies it to 2:144 as repeated seeing, glossing it as perhaps or often seeing the Prophet's face turn heavenward. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): Although قد with a present verb usually suggests rarity, here it is used by antithetical metaphor to suggest abundance. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (سيبويه): The frequency may be a lexical force of “قد” or an inference from the actual context; the latter account is attributed to Sibawayh. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Some take “قد” here to indicate rarity, arguing that infrequent glances better show the Prophet's perfect manners. Against: ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Al-Alusi objects that one upward glance is not called repeated turning; the word therefore conveys frequent turning in this context."}, {"id": "2:144/q01/p4", "position": "Qad confirms the occurrence.", "reasons": "BURHAN, d. 794 (author): Other grammarians analyze قد here as a particle of confirmation. BURHAN, d. 794 (author): قد confirms the occurrence of its verb with either present or past; in قد نرى and قد نعلم it can be understood with past reference. ITQAN, d. 911 (author): With an imperfect verb, قد can reduce the likelihood of an act or the extent of its object; some instead read it as certainty in examples such as قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه."}, {"id": "2:144/q01/p5", "position": "Frequency comes from the repeated turning, not from qad itself.", "reasons": "ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The word قد itself does not indicate frequency; repeated seeing is inferred from تقلب, since turning one's gaze entails repeated movements. {"id": "2:144/q13", "question": "What does the form and order of the promise convey?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:144/q13/p1", "position": "The promise answers an implicit oath, with emphatic lam.", "reasons": "ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The promise is made under an unspoken oath to emphasize that it will be fulfilled. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The fāʾ marks the result of what precedes and introduces an implicit oath, whose lām intensifies the certainty of the promise."}, {"id": "2:144/q13/p2", "position": "The promise precedes the command to reassure and delight him.", "reasons": "ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The promise precedes the command to delight the Prophet first by the response and again by its fulfillment; a promised result is also more reassuring than a sudden one.
